name: Microsoft Outlook
tagline: Register a Microsoft Entra app for Outlook and plug it into Composio. No review, but work tenants often need their admin's consent.

cost.asStated: Free. Publisher verification and its prerequisites have no charge.

steps.title: Choose the tenant that owns the app
instructions: Use a work account in your company's Microsoft Entra tenant with at least the Application Developer role.
Avoid a personal Microsoft account. Apps registered with one can't be publisher verified.
The app can't move to another tenant later. Pick the tenant your company will keep.

warnings.text: Publisher verification also rejects *.onmicrosoft.com publisher domains. Your tenant needs a DNS-verified custom domain.

steps.title: Register a new app
instructions: Open the Microsoft Entra admin center → Entra ID → App registrations → New registration.
Enter a Name. Users see it on the consent screen. You can change it later.
Supported account types: pick Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts. Covers work and outlook.com users.
Business users only? Pick Multiple Entra ID tenants. Single tenant blocks everyone outside your org.
Under Redirect URI, choose platform Web and paste the Composio callback below.
Click Register. Copy the Application (client) ID from Overview.
No Redirect URI field, or skipped it? Open Authentication → Add Redirect URI → Web.

fields.label: Name
fields.hint: Shown to users on the consent screen

fields.label: Supported account types
fields.value: Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts
fields.hint: Older UI: Accounts in any organizational directory and personal Microsoft accounts

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Case-sensitive. Must match your Composio auth config exactly

warnings.text: Redirect URIs are case-sensitive. Paste the callback exactly as shown.

problems.q: AADSTS50011: the redirect URI doesn't match
a: The app has no Web redirect URI equal to the one Composio sent.
Open Authentication and add the Composio callback under the Web platform, exactly as shown above.

problems.q: AADSTS50194: app isn't configured as a multitenant application
a: You registered the app as single tenant, so the shared /common sign-in endpoint refuses it.
Change Supported account types to a multi-tenant option.

problems.q: Personal outlook.com accounts can't sign in
a: The app only allows organizational accounts.
Switch Supported account types to Any Entra ID Tenant + Personal Microsoft accounts.

steps.title: Create a client secret
instructions: In your app, open Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret.
Add a description and pick an expiry. Maximum is 24 months. Microsoft recommends under 12.
Click Add, then copy the Value column, not the Secret ID.
The Value is shown once. Store it in a secret manager, never in git.
Set a reminder before it expires. Microsoft then rejects it with AADSTS7000222.

fields.label: Expires
fields.hint: Custom lifetimes are capped at 24 months

warnings.text: Microsoft recommends certificates over secrets in production. Composio's Outlook OAuth config takes a client secret.

problems.q: AADSTS7000215: Invalid client secret provided
a: Usually the Secret ID was pasted instead of the Value. Microsoft's own error says so.
Paste the Value into your Composio auth config. If you no longer have it, create a new secret.

problems.q: AADSTS7000222: the client secret keys are expired
a: Your secret passed its expiry date.
Create a new secret, update your Composio auth config, then delete the old secret.

problems.q: I closed the page before copying the Value
a: You can't view it again. Create a new client secret on the same page.
Delete the unused one so it doesn't linger.

steps.title: Add delegated Graph permissions
instructions: In your app, open API permissions → Add a permission → Microsoft Graph → Delegated permissions.
Add offline_access, Mail.Read and Mail.Send. User.Read is already there.
Add more only for tools you use, e.g. Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.ReadWrite, Contacts.ReadWrite.
Click Add permissions.
Don't pick Application permissions. They cover every mailbox in a tenant and always need admin consent.
Grant admin consent for <your tenant> only covers your own tenant, not your users' tenants.

fields.label: Starter permissions
fields.hint: Delegated. Trim or extend to match your Outlook tools

warnings.text: Without offline_access there is no refresh token, so connections stop when the access token expires.
Microsoft's default consent policy blocks user consent for Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite and Calendars. Expect admin consent in work tenants.

steps.unconfirmed: We couldn't see which scopes Composio's managed Outlook app requests. The starter set follows Composio's Outlook OAuth guide.

problems.q: A tool fails with a permissions error
a: The token lacks the Graph permission that tool needs, e.g. Calendars.ReadWrite for calendar tools.
Add it here and in your Composio auth config scopes, then have the user reconnect.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config
instructions: Open the Outlook toolkit in Composio and create an auth config.
Use the values below, then paste your Application (client) ID and the secret Value.
Make the scopes match the delegated permissions you added in Entra.
Save, then copy the auth config ID (ac_…) for the next step.

fields.label: Redirect URI
fields.hint: Must match the Web redirect URI in Entra exactly

fields.label: Scopes
fields.hint: Same list as API permissions in Entra

steps.unconfirmed: The link exists. We couldn't check, without logging in, whether it opens auth config creation directly. If not: Auth Configs → Create Auth Config.

problems.q: The link didn't open the Outlook toolkit
a: Open Auth Configs in the Composio dashboard and click Create Auth Config.
Pick Outlook, choose OAuth2, and turn on your own developer credentials.

steps.title: Use the auth config in your agent
instructions: Pass the auth config ID when you create a session. Your coding agent can paste this in.
Toolkits you don't list keep using Composio's managed auth.

problems.q: Connections still use Composio's app
a: The session must include authConfigs with your ac_… ID for outlook.
Toolkits not listed in authConfigs fall back to managed auth.

steps.title: Connect a test account
instructions: Start a connection for a test user and open the link.
Sign in with a work account from your own tenant first. The consent screen should show your app name.
Then try a personal outlook.com account and an account from another company.
Microsoft only checks the client ID after sign-in, so a typo shows up here, not earlier.
Until you're publisher verified, the consent screen says Unverified. That's expected.
Users already connected through managed auth must reconnect.
steps.unconfirmed: We didn't run a full connection. It needs a Composio API key and a real Microsoft sign-in.

problems.q: The consent screen still says Composio
a: The connection used the managed auth config. Pass your ac_… ID in the session.
Existing connections keep their old config. Delete and reconnect them.

problems.q: AADSTS700016: application wasn't found in the directory
a: The client ID in Composio doesn't match a registered app.
Copy the Application (client) ID from the app's Overview page again.

problems.q: A work user sees Need admin approval or AADSTS90094
a: Their tenant won't let users consent to what you request. Mail.Read is blocked by Microsoft's default policy.
Their admin has to grant consent. See the admin consent step below.

problems.q: AADSTS70008: the refresh token expired
a: Refresh tokens last 90 days by default and die after long inactivity or revocation.
Have the user reconnect.

steps.title: Join the AI Cloud Partner Program
steps.when: Only for publisher verification, and only if your company has no Partner One ID yet.
instructions: Enroll your company in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program in Partner Center, signed in with a work account.
Use an employee business email for verification, not a personal or free email account.
Microsoft checks your email, identity, employment and business registration. Upload documents if asked.
Note the Partner One ID of the partner global account (PGA). A location ID won't work.

wait.asStated: In most cases three to five business days. Some checks take longer.

problems.q: The verification email never arrived
a: Add microsoft.com as a safe sender and check junk mail.
Resend the code from Verification Summary → Contact Info in Partner Center.

steps.title: Verify your publisher
steps.when: Recommended before users outside your own tenant connect.
instructions: Sign in with MFA as Application Administrator or Cloud Application Administrator.
In your app, open Branding & properties and set the Publisher domain to a DNS-verified domain.
It, or another DNS-verified domain in your tenant, must match your Partner Center verification email domain.
Select Add Partner ID to verify publisher, enter your Partner One ID, then Verify and save.
In Partner Center you also need Partner Admin or Accounts Admin.
A blue verified badge appears next to the publisher name, usually within minutes.

warnings.text: Verification doesn't remove admin consent for Mail.Read in tenants on Microsoft's default consent policy.

problems.q: NoPublisherDomainOnApplication or PublisherDomainMismatch
a: Set a Publisher domain under Branding & properties. *.onmicrosoft.com doesn't qualify.
It must match the domain of your Partner Center primary contact's email, or be a verified domain in your tenant.

problems.q: MPNAccountNotFoundOrNoAccess or MPNGlobalAccountNotFound
a: NotFoundOrNoAccess: usually your user lacks an admin role on that Partner Center account, or the app's tenant isn't linked to it.
GlobalAccountNotFound: you entered a partner location ID. Use the partner global account's Partner One ID.

steps.title: Get admin consent in your user's tenant
steps.when: When a work user sees Need admin approval. Common: Microsoft's default policy blocks user consent for Mail.Read.
instructions: Send their admin the URL below with their tenant and your client ID. They sign in and approve.
{tenant} is their tenant ID or a verified domain. organizations uses the admin's own tenant.
The admin needs Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator.
Or in their Entra: Enterprise apps → All applications → your app → Permissions → Grant admin consent.
If their tenant has the admin consent workflow on, users can request approval from the consent screen.
After approval, the user starts a fresh connection with their own account. The admin doesn't connect for them.

warnings.text: Microsoft's managed default policy blocks user consent for Mail.Read, Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.* and more. New tenants use it.
A June–July 2026 rollout added Contacts.ReadWrite, Tasks.* and People.Read to that blocked list.
Unverified multi-tenant apps asking beyond basic sign-in get stepped up to admin consent in other tenants.
Personal Microsoft accounts (outlook.com) consent to Mail.Read themselves. No admin involved.

steps.unconfirmed: We didn't approve an app in a real tenant. Where the admin lands after approving isn't verified.

problems.q: Users get AADSTS90094 or Need admin approval
a: Their tenant blocks user consent for a permission you request, or flagged your unverified app as risky.
An admin grants consent with the URL above. Publisher verification avoids the risky-app step-up.

problems.q: AADSTS65001 after the admin approved
a: No consent exists for this user and app. The admin may have approved in a different tenant.
Check {tenant} in the URL was the user's tenant, then approve again.

problems.q: The admin doesn't see Grant admin consent
a: Their role is too low. They need Cloud Application Administrator, Application Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator.

problems.q: The admin's mailbox got connected instead of the user's
a: The admin signed in during the user's connection attempt.
Delete that connection. After tenant-wide consent, the user reconnects with their own account.
